STRUCTURE BEATS STAMINA. EVERY TIME.

Six focused weeks. One feedback loop.

Six months of random applying produces exhaustion — not offers. This sprint turns your search into a weekly system: act, measure, adjust. Each week has one focus, a clear checklist and a Friday self-check so you can see what is working.

By Week 5 you should have enough activity to see patterns. Week 6 is about closing an offer or diagnosing the exact stage that needs fixing.

05

PIPELINE MANAGEMENT

WEEK 5 · TRACK, FOLLOW UP, DOUBLE DOWN

CHECKLIST

FEEDBACK LOOP

Stop guessing. Use the numbers to decide where to spend Week 6.

06

OFFER OR PIVOT

WEEK 6 · CLOSE IT OR DIAGNOSE IT

IF YOU HAVE AN OFFER

  • Negotiate with a researched number.
  • Don't accept on the spot.
  • Ask for 24 hours to review the package.
  • Anchor to the market rate, not to relief.
IF YOU HAVE NO OFFER

Audit the system, not the effort. Which stage breaks: resume, outreach or interview?

YOUR PIPELINE SNAPSHOT
APPLICATIONS
CONVERSATIONS
INTERVIEWS

Use the numbers as diagnostic signals, not as a reason to chase volume. If applications get no replies, inspect the resume. If you get interviews but no offers, inspect the interview stage.
